title: Choosing units for maintainable responsive layouts
learningObjectives: Explain choosing units for maintainable responsive layouts and choose suitable CSS values for a responsive layout.

understand.concept: Choose CSS units according to the relationship you want to express. Use rem for root-relative typography and spacing scales, percentages for property-specific parent-relative sizing, fr for grid track shares, and viewport or container units when the design should respond to those regions. Fixed CSS pixels remain useful for small details and boundaries.
understand.whyItMatters: There is no single best unit for every property. Consider user zoom, text enlargement, intrinsic content, available space, and the component's context. Prefer constraints and flexible layouts over rigid dimensions.
understand.analogy: Choosing a unit is choosing the ruler that matches the relationship you want to preserve.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; actual sizing follows CSS value resolution and layout algorithms.

practise.guidedTask: Build a responsive article using rem, %, ch, and clamp(). Explain why each unit is appropriate.
practise.independentTask: Create a small responsive component using the concept. Test narrow and wide viewports, long text, and browser zoom.
hints: Inspect computed values in developer tools.
Change one unit at a time.
Avoid fixed dimensions that unnecessarily clip content.

questions.prompt: What should guide your choice of a CSS unit?
options: The relationship and behaviour the design needs
A universal unit that always means pixels
questions.answer: The relationship and behaviour the design needs
questions.explanation: Units should be chosen according to their reference, content, and responsive behaviour.

questions.prompt: How should you choose a CSS unit?
options: Match the unit to the desired sizing relationship
Always use px for every property
questions.answer: Match the unit to the desired sizing relationship
questions.explanation: The unit's reference and responsive behaviour should match the design requirement.
